- [x] **W40.i3-fu-shots — iOS E2E screenshots show one stale frame [S]** · §W40 — verification phase (lane: processor) (uses: build). SHIPPED 2026-10-22.
  Cause: `CameraPreview.makeUIView` set `AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer.session` inside SwiftUI's layout pass once
  `camera.authorized` turned true. That commits the session on the main thread and waits in a nested run loop
  (`_buildAndRunGraph:` → `AVRunLoopCondition`) for its graph, which on the camera-less simulator did not finish
  while the run lasted. The driver, uploads and timers ran on inside that loop, but no frame was committed. A
  temporary probe (display-link and run-loop counts, the key window's own layer tree) showed the app stale while the
  framebuffer was live, and a probe run that aborted gave the stack. Fix: `CameraController.hasCamera` (nil until
  configured); the capture screen attaches the preview only when the session has a back-camera input, and
  otherwise says "No camera on this device." (the QR scanner already had this guard). `e2e-phone-mac.sh --ios` now
  fails the phone side unless the connected shot and every page's shot differ. Two reruns PASS, with 5 distinct
  shots each, every page's thumbnail visible. Evidence: `verification/evidence/capture/W40.i3-ios-e2e.md` §W40.i3-fu-shots.
  <!-- /W40.i3-fu-shots -->

- [x] **W40.fix-notes-block-marker-in-text — a line of note text that reads as a block header becomes one on the next read [S · S4]** · §W40 — verification phase: prove the Suite works (owner-approved 2026-10-04) (lane: notes) (uses: build). Found by `W40.e6` 2026-10-20; reproduction: `ArchiveNotesTests/FrontMatterMutationFuzzTests.blockHeaderLineInTextKnownIssue` (`withKnownIssue`). A block whose markdown holds the line `<!-- block: freeform -->` saves it verbatim; `BlockParser.parse` then splits there, so the line vanishes from the text and the block becomes two. The format has no escape. Either escape such a line on save (and unescape on read), or refuse it in the editor; remove the known issue when done. Tier-2: it changes what a Notes save writes.
  SHIPPED 2026-10-28. The format now has an escape (`execution-plans/archive-notes/00-overview.md` §6): a line of text that begins with `<!-- block:` after any number of backslashes is written with one more backslash and read back with one fewer (`BlockParser.escapingHeaderLines` / `unescapingHeaderLines`, applied by `serialize`/`parse` to the leading prose and every block's text; a headerless block's opener line is left alone). That is a bijection, so the operator's own backslashes survive, and one backslash before `<` is CommonMark's escape, so the editor shows the line as typed. Editor side: `MarkdownBridge.serialize` escapes each body segment the same way, the bridge's no-block parse renders the unescaped text, and `EditorPassageSource.snapshotMarkdown` unescapes because its output becomes one block's text. `ExtractBuilder.flattenedNestedHeaders` is removed: with the escape a nested header line cannot become a block, and the stripping now only dropped the operator's line from an extract (found by the Tier-2 review). Tests: the known issue is now `blockHeaderLineInTextStaysText` (LF/CR/CRLF, backslash runs, a combining mark after the marker, mid-line, leading text and a sourced block), plus two editor round trips (byte-stable second save, code fence, a freshly typed line); the fuzz generator no longer avoids header lines; the extract tests assert the line is kept as text and reloads as one note-passage block. Notes unit bundle green, 1006 + 225 tests. Not changed: pasted text over the large-paste threshold is read as on-disk Markdown, so a pasted `\\<!-- block:` line shows one backslash fewer (cosmetic). No migration: nothing to migrate.
  <!-- /W40.fix-notes-block-marker-in-text -->

The recogniser's CER cannot gate (McCATMuS reads these hands at 40-60% CER: 4-5 pages kept). The Mac holds idle usbmux tunnels into a 127.0.0.1:48628 listener in the app. The app's 127.0.0.1:48629 relay splices each URLSession connection into a tunnel, so `MacClient`, the outbox and `CaptureServer` are unchanged and Cable is a third connect mode on the same QR. Rejected: the Mac pulling (a second protocol and ack path), an HTTP client written over the tunnel, any documented Apple route (none exists), and QR-less pairing (later). An `AC1` nonce→HMAC(lanToken) handshake stops an app on the phone posing as the Mac and getting a photo deleted. Bridged connections get their own auth-throttle key. A locked or backgrounded phone pauses uploads with no loss, as Wi-Fi does today. Recovery comes from a 2 s top-up and 20 s idle expiry on the Mac, and re-created listeners on `.active`. Undocumented-service risk: measured on macOS 26.6 with no phone, `ListDevices`, `ReadBUID` and `Listen` answered and `Connect` to a missing device returned Result 2. Only the Mac uses the private protocol; a host probe will catch a change. Personal Hotspot is kept as a workaround only (carrier/MDM, cellular routing, S-037, the rejected-transport rule). S-037 is fixed in the build, including Android's empty-host parse. Testable without a phone: a fake usbmuxd that decodes the byte-swapped port, host tests of the relay, and a simulator E2E over the shared loopback. The real `Connect`, trust, lock recovery and ATS on a device are left to W40.i5-usb/W40.i4. No proof was needed before the build. An adversarial review found 9 defects in the first draft, all folded in: the impostor tunnel, byte order, no-EOF stale tunnels, concurrency, Android's empty host, the stored port, close-truncation, the shared throttle, and socket rules. Build split: W40.i-usb-mac, W40.i-usb-app (parallel), then W40.i-usb-build (E2E + docs). No bench cache used; $0 spent.
  <!-- /W40.i-usb-design -->

- [x] **W40.i-usb-mac — the Mac end of the iPhone cable route: usbmux tunnels into the app [M]** · §W40 — verification phase: prove the Suite works (owner-approved 2026-10-04) (lane: processor) (uses: build) — Tier-2 (`Net/`). Build `Net/USBMuxBridge.swift` per `execution-plans/iphone-usb.md` §2 and §8.1: usbmuxd codec (port in network byte order), a dedicated Listen socket, one fresh socket per tunnel, four idle tunnels per USB-attached iPhone topped up every 2 s, 20 s idle expiry, the `AC1` HMAC handshake answer, an end-of-stream-forwarding splice into `CaptureServer`, a separate auth-throttle key for bridged connections; the pane and QR caption cable line; the S-037 QR fix (a QR whenever the server listens, host empty if no address) and Android's empty-host parse with its test; a fake usbmuxd, a test driver and script; `scripts/usbmux-probe.sh`.
  SHIPPED 2026-10-31. Result: `Net/USBMuxBridge.swift` keeps four idle usbmux tunnels per USB-attached iPhone open into the app's 48628 (fresh socket per `Connect`, the Result read to its exact length so the phone's hello is never swallowed, top-up every 2 s whatever `Connect` returned, idle expiry at 20 s less up to a quarter so a burst-filled pool is not replaced in one tick, `Detached` closes every tunnel, a lost Listen socket reconnects every 5 s and leaves spliced requests to finish), answers `AC1` + nonce with HMAC-SHA256(lanToken, nonce), and on the first request byte splices to a new loopback-only `CaptureServer` cable listener (127.0.0.1, system port, no Bonjour), forwarding each end of stream as a half-close. A refusal the server sends before reading the body (it then closes with the body unread, a reset) still reaches the phone: a failed read from the server ends only that direction. The cable listener keys its failed-auth throttle `cable:<device>` from the port the bridge registered (`CablePeers`), never the fail-open "unknown", so loopback, `adb reverse` and the cable no longer share 127.0.0.1's bucket. Wired from `CaptureSession.cableListenerDidStart`/`Stop` (only the current listener reports, so a quick stop then start cannot stop the new bridge). The pane gains a cable line (connected / scan the QR / open Archive Capture / Cable route unavailable); "connected" needs a tunnel the phone kept 1 s after the answer, so a phone paired to another Mac never reads connected. S-037: the QR shows whenever the server listens; with no en0/en1 address its host falls back to a pairable other interface (not utun/ipsec/awdl/llw, not 169.254), else empty, and the pane says to pair over the cable or Cloud. Android parses an empty-host QR for Wired and Cloud and refuses it for Wi-Fi with a message (`MacEndpoint.hasHost`, `MacEndpointQrTest.emptyHostQr_parsesForWiredAndCloud`; Android unit 85/85). The current iPhone app still rejects an empty-host QR (its `MacEndpoint` returns nil for a blank host); `W40.i-usb-app` adds it, as planned. Tests: `scripts/fake-usbmuxd.py` (plist framing, decodes `PortNumber` with the swap, FakeAttach/FakeDetach/FakeStats controls), `USBMuxBridgeTestDriver` + `scripts/test-usbmux-bridge.sh` (43 checks, 12 of 12 runs green on the final code: codec 48628 → 0xF4BD, the pool of four, a Wi-Fi-synced device ignored, a 512 KB reply the server closes at once arriving whole alone and four at a time, expiry with no EOF, silent / wrong-hello / other-Mac tunnels, refused `Connect` retried, detach, the 401-before-body case, the cable's own throttle key both ways on a real `CaptureServer`, the cable listener refused on the LAN address), and `scripts/usbmux-probe.sh` (the real usbmuxd: ListDevices, ReadBUID, Listen → 0, Connect to no device → 2; ~50 ms); both are health-gate steps and the bridge test is in the sanitizer and mutation driver lists. Mutations: sending the port unswapped fails 4 checks; an abortive close on the server's end of stream fails the whole-reply checks (524,288 of 524,350 bytes). A graceful close after the last send completes is indistinguishable from forwarding the EOF here, which is fine. Tier-2 review (Opus, read-only): no HIGH; its six actionable findings fixed in this commit (registration proven on the real path, the listener stop/start race, staggered expiry, the early-refusal drain, the registered port kept on the tunnel, the pairable fallback host). Adjacent: `test-manifest-persistence`, `test-recovery`, `test-network-session` ALL PASS. No bench cache used.

Safety §11 requires partial failures be surfaced, as `mark` does (`Marked 1; 1 could not update.`). Progress in `W40.audit-ledger-undo` (checkpoint e4fe101c): failures are counted, named and announced; the strict expected-failure wrapper is removed. Durable undo consumes the whole group before any inverse so an interrupted occurrence inverse cannot replay. **Remaining scope:** decide and implement whether a failed member whose cause may pass can be retried safely, with per-member durable accounting; an identity mismatch must never retry against a replacement. Do not repeat the reporting fix or remove the group-consumption safety guard.

A member that failed for any cause but an identity refusal is re-recorded after the attempt as one new undo group (`AuditLedger.keepForRetry`, new `retryOf`/`attempt` entry fields, one synchronized append), and the status ends "Undo again to retry." The group-consumption guard stays: `beginUndo` still consumes the whole batch before any inverse, so a crash before the retry record loses the retry and never replays. Retry is safe even after a partly landed write because `applyOccurrence(undoing:)` is clamped to the pre-change counts (W45.undo-still-applied). Identity refusals (replaced, gone, outside the archive) are never retried; three attempts at most (`undoAttemptLimit`), so a lasting cause cannot block older undo. Found in self-review: once one of a file's writes in the group fails, its older writes are skipped and kept with it, re-recorded in write order (otherwise a retry could put back a tag the step removed). Tests: `UndoDurabilityTests.testAFailedMemberWhoseCauseMayPassCanBeRetried` (immutable-flag lock, relaunch, retry touches only the failed file), `testARetryIsDroppedAfterTheAttemptLimit`, `testOnlyAnIdentityRefusalIsNeverRetried`, `LedgerUndoHistoryTests.testARetriedSameFileStepStillUndoesInReverseOrder` (mutation-checked: without the write-order re-record it fails with X, Y left).   A template body the store refuses now survives quit, a crash and its window closing, as a note's does. `NotesModel.setTemplateBody`
  runs one template's saves in call order and settles the held refused body inside each save; `EditorFlushRegistry.trackTemplateBody`
  (called after every template save) registers the held body under the TEMPLATE's id (flush = `retryTemplateBody`, draft =
  `unsavedTemplateBody`), copies it to the `UnsavedDraftVault` at once, and drops it once it saves. Quit retries it and is refused while
  it fails; the pane's teardown closes it through `paneClosed` (retry, copy, ask). Keyed by template, so a closed window never writes an
  older buffer over a newer save from another window. The Tier-2 review found two more holes, both fixed here: `flushAll` iterated a
  snapshot, so a body refused for the FIRST time inside quit's own flush let quit proceed (it now flushes entries registered mid-pass);
  and deleting a template silently deleted its refused body's emergency copy (it now stands, as a trashed note's does). Scratch functional
  tests `TemplateFailedSaveTests` (8): read-only `Templates/<uuid>/` refusal, quit/close/keep/switch/order/first-refusal-at-quit/delete.

Make the template save report its refusal (a checked seam, or `save` returning the Bool into `persist`) so the template pane keeps the draft, copies it to the `UnsavedDraftVault` and refuses quit exactly as note panes do; the pane's teardown must then close through `paneClosed`, not `deregister`.   (lane: notes) [S · S2]. `ZoteroClient.fetchCSLviaLocalAPI` now reads `csljson` as a string holding a CSL array
  (decoded by `parseCSLArray`), an array, or an object, and only a validated dictionary reaches
  `JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject:)` (`decodeCSLObject`), so no Zotero answer can raise the Objective-C

Every page of a retried segment failed with errorCode 402 and the message "Rate limit exceeded. Try again later." Google's own reply was HTTP 402, status RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, "Your prepayment credits are depleted. Please go to AI Studio…". `GeminiClient.parseErrorResponse` maps any RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED to the rate-limit text before looking at the status code, so a billing stop reads as a wait-and-retry. `KeyValidator` already knows 402 means billing (`.needsBilling`). Fix: a 402 from any client says the account needs credit or billing, names the provider and its billing page, and is not retried automatically; RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with 429 stays the rate-limit text. Unit tests on both bodies for Gemini, and the same check for the OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic clients. Re-check needs no phone. SHIPPED 2026-10-31. A 402 from any client now reads "Your <Provider> account is out of credit or needs billing set up. Add credit or billing at <billing page>, then run these pages again." with the provider's own words kept after it (`billingStatusMessage`, `OCR/OCRErrorMessages.swift`; billing pages from `ProviderKeySpec`). Gemini checks it before RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, so 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED stays the rate-limit text; OpenAI-compatible names OpenAI or OpenRouter by endpoint (a gateway gets the provider-neutral wording), including OpenRouter's 200-with-error code 402; Anthropic keeps code "402" whatever the body type; Mistral too. `isRetryableError` refuses code 402 outright, and in segmentation a 402 is fatal (every window) instead of the usage limit. Proof: `ArchiveProcessor/scripts/test-provider-errors.sh` (ProviderErrorTestDriver, canned bodies, $0) 40/40 pass; `test-openrouter.sh`'s 402 check still passes (its one red, the GLM figures, is pre-existing and filed as W40.fix-openrouter-glm-figures-check). No bench cache used.

  reported when every kept segment is unprocessed). The shipping session's traced every exit from

- [x] **W40.fix-processor-live-settings-per-run — a Settings change reaches Live Capture only after the Processor is relaunched, and nothing says so [S · S3]** · §W40 — verification phase (lane: processor) (uses: build) — SHIPPED 2026-11-01.
  Original report: Owner session iphone-1, 2026-10-31 (`verification/sessions/iphone-1-returned.md`). With the gateway switched on in Settings, Retry, Clear, Finish and Start all kept using direct Gemini: `CaptureSession.activateProcessingIfNeeded` snapshots `SessionProcessingConfig.fromDefaults()` once, on first activity, and `processingMode` is never reset in an app run, so the route is fixed until a relaunch. The snapshot is deliberate (mid-session changes must not reach a running session), but it should end with the session: re-snapshot once Finish or Clear has emptied it, and show the session's route (provider and model, or gateway) in the Live Capture pane so a stale one is visible. Test: change the route between two sessions in one run and assert the second uses it.
  **Fix.** `CaptureSession.releaseSettingsSnapshotIfEmpty()` drops the session's snapshot (`processingMode` back to `.undecided`, `config` nil, `settingsLocked` off) once Finish or Clear has emptied the session: no photo left, no Clear marker pending, and for live `LiveCaptureProcessor.holdsNoSessionWork` (nothing staged, in flight, finalized-but-unstaged, pending, finishing or blocked). It runs at the end of `finalize`'s Task, of `clearSession()` and of `CaptureSession.clear()`. The next page's `activateProcessingIfNeeded` then reads Settings again and re-arms through `activate`. A session that still holds anything keeps its snapshot, so a retry or a second Finish reuses the route its pages began on. The Processing box now says "This session: <route> · <tagging>" (route = `retryBackendDescription`: Local Agent, then gateway, then provider·model; `summary` used to name the provider even on the gateway route) and "A Settings change applies after Finish or Clear." The per-row provider·model line uses the same route. The pane's live/stage branches (`liveMode`, the Process → button, the output-folder control) follow the session's own mode once it has one, not Settings as they are now.
  **Tier-2 review** (Opus subagent) found one real defect, fixed before shipping: a Clear whose LAST capture-manifest write fails keeps its committed marker in memory. Releasing then would let the next page's `activate` → `loadStagingManifest` finish that committed Clear again and Trash the page that triggered it. The release now also requires `clearPhase` and `clearToken` to be nil. Other points it checked and found safe: every `processingMode == .live` guard stays covered while work is held, re-running `activate` re-buys no OCR and files nothing twice, and `clearGeneration` still makes a stale `finalizeSegment` bail. Pre-existing and left alone: a stale Clear marker carried to a relaunch has the same shape.
  **Test.** Recovery driver Test 32 (`scripts/test-recovery.sh`, $0) runs the real ingest → finalize → Clear paths with the OCR stub recording each page's route (`_recoveryTestOCRRoutes`): Finish releases the snapshot; a route changed between sessions (direct → gateway) is the next session's route; a change mid-session does not reach it; Clear releases it and the next page takes the new route; a Clear whose final write fails keeps the snapshot, and a completing Clear releases it. Its pages are real JPEGs: a placeholder page keeps its source photo (W23.h5), and a kept photo leaves the session non-empty, so the snapshot rightly stays (which is why Test 30, with fake bytes, still reads `.live` after its Finish). A test-armed session re-arms through `_recoveryTestBeginLive` with `recoveryTestSettings` standing in for Settings, never `activate`, whose legacy prune is unsafe under a redirected backup root. So the production re-`activate` is covered by review, not by this test.
  No bench cache used.

  the staging-dir choice and `resume(stagingDir:config:)`, which no longer feeds pages of staged or filed groups to
  `photoIngested` (that only posted the late-page warning, which the resume would have shown on every relaunch). Tier-2
  review found one regression in the first draft and it is fixed: the resume took the Settings snapshot when the pane opened
  rather than at the operator's first action, so a route changed after the relaunch (the owner's 402 key, then the gateway)
  would have been ignored by Retry; the resumed snapshot is now provisional (`refreshProvisionalSnapshotIfUnused`) and the
  first Retry or page re-reads Settings, after which it is the session's as W40.fix-processor-live-settings-per-run decided.

- [x] **W40.fix-reader-ledger-durability — the undo ledger's forward records are best-effort, unbounded and not fsynced [S · S3 · Tier-2]** · §W40 — verification phase · SHIPPED 2026-11-03
  Original scope: (lane: reader) (uses: build). Owner, 2026-10-31, from `ArchiveReader/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` §"W40.audit-ledger-undo":
  process death could lose a missing forward record and its barrier; ledger growth unbounded; forward appends not fsynced.
  Built: each forward action is write-ahead journalled in `Core/AuditLedger.swift`. `TagWriter.journalledWrite` flushes an
  `actionIntent` (`F_FULLFSYNC`, fallback `fsync` only on ENOTSUP/EINVAL) inside coordination once the transform decides to
  write, so a no-op or refused write journals nothing; `withContext` closes the action with a flushed `actionDone` unless a
  record failed or a write failed verification. An unclosed intent is a permanent barrier in `undoGroups` (that action and
  everything older). Records between are not flushed one by one; the done's flush covers them (two flushes per action,
  however many files). Appends use `open(2)` `O_APPEND`. The live file is cut into numbered 4 MiB segments that are kept
  (§12 is append-only; no pruning, so the disk still keeps ~1 KB per changed file; ask the owner before any retention);
  undo reads newest first and stops at a barrier or a full 100-group window. An unreadable existing file, or a segment cut
  by another copy during the read, offers nothing. Residual, stated in KNOWN_ISSUES: an intent that cannot be written at
  all followed by process death before storage recovers. Tests: `LedgerJournalTests` (11, crash cases simulated by
  dropping a scratch ledger's last lines); whole Reader unit bundle 546 green, no new warnings; write-surface lint
  allowance swapped (the `FileHandle(forWritingTo:)` line is gone, the segment `moveItem` added; `open(2)` is not a
  spelling the lint matches). Adversarial review (opus): no HIGH; its MEDIUM findings (read failure skipping the live
  file, two-copy overwrites, a failed rename disabling the ledger) and LOW ones (fsync fallback, same-group nesting,
  post-close writes, unverified write closing normally) were all fixed. R-46 stays fixed-pending-recheck. No migration
  written: there is no production ledger to migrate. Bench cache: not used.
  <!-- /W40.fix-reader-ledger-durability -->

- [x] **W40.fix-reader-prose-paragraphs — Copy Cleaned for Prose finds the paragraph breaks the OCR left unmarked [M · S3]** · §W40 — verification phase: prove the Suite works (owner-approved 2026-10-04) (lane: reader) (uses: build) — SHIPPED 2026-11-04.
  From the owner's Reader guided session 1 (verification/sessions/reader-1-returned.md row 19, his first priority): the OCR sometimes gives no blank line at a paragraph break, so Copy Cleaned for Prose ran two paragraphs into one. The plan line pointed at a SUITE_TODO entry that was never filed (the session-return commit filed no fix items); this entry is the whole record.
  Fix: `PDFPaneController.layoutLines` reads the selection's lines and their boxes from PDFKit (`selectionsByLine`, geometry only), and `CopyTextCleaner.clean(_:lines:options:)` inserts a blank line before each line the layout says starts a paragraph, then cleans as before. Signs, judged per block (one page, one column, three lines or more) in the block's median line height: a gap over 1.6× the usual line spacing; a first-line indent over 1.2 em that neither neighbour shares (so a quoted or hanging block is not split line by line); a line before that stops over a quarter of the width short after `.`/`!`/`?`/`:`, or over half short ending in anything but a comma or hyphen, when the line starts with a capital, digit or quote. Typewritten pages are ragged, so shortness alone never breaks; a hyphen-split word never breaks. If PDFKit's lines do not match the text's non-blank lines one for one, the text is cleaned exactly as before. Options ▸ Copying text has a new toggle (on by default). On the Processor's typeset text page only the short-line sign can fire (the OCR text there carries no indent or extra spacing); the image page's text layer gets all three.
  Tests: CopyTextCleanerTests +12 (indent, short line, ragged line kept, wider gap, indented block, hyphen, existing blank lines not doubled, mismatch fallback, option off, column jump, a PDF drawn line by line through PDFKit, a typeset text page with a wrapped line); Reader unit bundle 558 tests, 0 failures (DeepLinkTests skipped as usual). Not checked on real corpus pages: the owner's next Reader pack (W40.g1-reader-2) is where it meets real OCR. No bench cache used.

- [x] **W40.fix-notes-editor-lines — Return adds blank lines, Backspace joins lines, and Bulleted List makes a list, every time [M · S2]** · §W40 (lane: notes) — SHIPPED 2026-11-05. Found by the owner's Notes guided session 1 (`verification/sessions/notes-1-returned.md`, rows 8, 10; ledger N-12). Cause, measured on unmodified main: on the empty last line, `insertNewline`, `deleteBackward`, Tab/Shift-Tab and the block toggles read the paragraph's kind at `storage.length`, which raised `NSRangeException`. AppKit swallowed it, so a second Return, a Backspace there, and Bulleted List on a fresh line did nothing; it went away once anything else was typed. Separately, the save wrote every Return as a paragraph break, so after a reselect one Return reopened as a blank line, three as one, and a blank line deleted with Backspace came back. List items drew no marker at all. Fix: `EditorFormatting.blockKind(at:in:)` falls back to the typing attributes on that line, and toggles with no selection set them. `MarkdownBridge.plainLines` writes a run of newlines by its count: one is a hard break `\`, two a paragraph break, each past two a hard break starting the next paragraph. Next to raw HTML the break is a paragraph break, and `-`, `=` and `<` are escaped at a line start. The Styler shows block boundaries (heading, list, quote, code) as one newline, and the serializer writes a blank line between blocks of different kinds. Return at a heading's end starts text, and at its start leaves text above. Backspace joining a line takes the line above's kind. Block-kind changes go through shouldChangeText/didChangeText, so they can be undone and they save. Adjacent headings stay separate. Raw HTML is written verbatim (it gained escapes on every save before). `ListMarkers` and `EditorTextView.drawListMarkers` draw •/◦/▪ and numbers, with a DEBUG probe `an.editor.test.listMarkers`. Tier-2 (the serializer writes the note file): an Opus adversarial review found 8 problems and a second pass checked the fixes; all fixed with tests. Verified: `EditorLinesTests` (25, through the real text view: type, reselect, type again); unit bundle green, no new warnings; VM `EditorLinesUITests` and `EditorLinesStackedUITests`: rows 8 and 10 with real keystrokes, ⇧⌘U, the Format menu and the toolbar, reselect, relaunch. `WritingJourneyUITests` (both layouts) and `VisualPolishUITests` also passed in the VM; screenshots show the bullets. Promise-test change: the d9 journey types two Returns for its paragraph checks. Remaining limits, which Markdown has no form for, are listed in ArchiveNotes/KNOWN_ISSUES.md. Ledger N-12 is `fixed-pending-recheck`; the recheck is `W40.g2-notes-2`. Evidence: `verification/evidence/notes/W40.fix-notes-editor-lines.md`. No bench cache used.
  <!-- /W40.fix-notes-editor-lines -->
- [x] **W40.fix-notes-bold-space — bold that ends in a space stays bold [S · S3]** · §W40 (lane: notes) — SHIPPED 2026-11-05. Found by the owner's Notes guided session 1 (`verification/sessions/notes-1-returned.md`, row 11; ledger N-12): a bold "Day " saved as `**Day **`, which CommonMark does not read as bold (emphasis does not close after a space), so it reopened as literal asterisks and the next save escaped them to `\*\*Day \*\*`. Fix: `MarkdownBridge.wrapEmphasis` moves whitespace at a run's edges outside the `*`/`**`/`***` delimiters, and a run that is only whitespace is written plain. Links and inline code were already safe (`[Day ](url)` and a one-sided space in a code span both keep their meaning). Not covered: emphasis whose edge is punctuation next to a letter (`a**"b"**c`) is also not read as emphasis by CommonMark; nobody has hit it and Markdown has no clean form for it. Verified: `FormattingActionTests.emphasisEndingInSpaceRoundTrips` (bold, italic, bold italic: save, reopen styled with no asterisks, second save identical), `boldStartingWithSpaceKeepsTheSpaceOutside`, `boldSpaceAloneWritesNoDelimiters`; Notes unit bundle green (1099 tests), no new warnings. Ledger N-12 stays `fixed-pending-recheck`; the recheck is `W40.g2-notes-2`. No bench cache used.

Dragging a note over the folder tree highlights folders erratically, depending on the pointer's position: the highlighted row must be the row the drop will land in.
  SHIPPED 2026-11-05. Cause, measured in the VM: a sidebar label is 16 pt of its 32 pt row, and the 8 pt above and
  below it belonged to the level's `ForEach.onMove`, whose List-drawn gap targets only reorder; of the label, the top
  and bottom quarters reordered too, so only an 8 pt band nested, and the List's own highlight came and went as the
  pointer crossed the dead gaps. XCUITest's synthesized quick drag nested even before the fix (baseline run), so the
  hand's failure was the aim, not the gesture. Fix (`NotesFolderTreeView`): no `onMove`; each row's drop area reaches
  8 pt past the label (`NotesFolderRowDropTarget.reach`, layout unchanged); every pointer move resolves one target —
  row, before/into/after (`NotesItemDrag.dropZone`) and what is dragged, read from the drag pasteboard
  (`NotesItemDrag.dragKind`) — which the app draws (an accent outline for into, a line for beside) and the drop
  performs, so the highlight is the landing row by construction. A folder over itself or into its descendant resolves
  to nothing: no highlight, a refused drop. Below an open folder the line means its first child from either row; a
  nest opens the folder it went into. Two traps found on the way: a SwiftUI folder drag lists the `.ownProcess`
  folder type on the drag pasteboard but answers nil for its data (checkpoint 1 refused every folder drop until the
  id was read from the text), and SwiftUI sends the dropped row a late update that re-lit the highlight and left it
  on (seen in the video; a finished drag's pasteboard change count is now ignored). Not handled: a drag cancelled
  with no `dropExited` could leave a highlight until the next drag; a reorder is still one `moveFolder` per sibling.
  An open parent's outline row reads identifier `an.sidebar.folder-an.sidebar.folder`, label "Ideas, 3" (SwiftUI's
  DisclosureGroup merge); the new test matches it by prefix. Tests: unit `NotesItemDragTests` (dropZone, dragKind;
  1104 unit tests green); VM, 10/10 with screen video — new `testE2_QuickFolderDragOntoMiddleNests`,
  `testE2_FolderDropBelowAnOpenFolderBecomesItsFirstChild`, `testE2_NoteDropOnAnyPartOfAFolderRowFilesIntoIt`
  (4 pt above and below the label, each drop checked for no left-over highlight through the DEBUG seam
  `an.sidebar.test.dropTarget`), plus the E2 folder tests, G18, G7 and the W9 table drag. Ledger N-26 →
  `fixed-pending-recheck`; the owner's hand rechecks it in notes-2. No bench cache used.

  answer, never on an unreachable or slow Zotero; the probe (`GET /api/`, then BBT `api.ready`, 3 s) is a status signal
  only and a successful fetch refreshes it; BBT citations use `item.bibliography` with the style URI (`item.export`
  takes a translator); `ClientError` is a `LocalizedError` (switched off in Notes, unreachable, timed out, local API
  off, item not found, unreadable), each a sentence naming what to check; a failed inspector chip shows the reason
  (`an.zotero.failure.<key>`); an attached block is inserted with a pending marker and filled with its citation when
  Zotero answers (`Coordinator.fillPendingCitation`), and a failure says why on the status line.
  Tests: unit bundle 1115 green; new `ZoteroClientErrorTextTests`, `fetchSucceedsAfterAFailedProbe`,
  `probeNeverListsTheLibrary`, `testSilentServerIsTimedOut`, BBT `item.bibliography`. VM: G11, G15 (now also waits for

- [x] **W40.fix-reader-preview-image-speed — the preview's image arrives after its text [S · S4]** · §W40 (lane: reader) (uses: build) — Found by the owner's Reader guided session 1, 2026-11-04 (`verification/sessions/reader-1-returned.md`, row 17): Selection ▸ Preview showed the text at once and the image a moment later. Measure where the time goes, then prefetch or render a downscaled image first; report the before and after times. SHIPPED 2026-11-06.
  **Where the time went (measured, twelve corpus PDFs copied read-only to a scratch folder):** opening the PDF takes under 1 ms and its text 0.2–15 ms, but PDFKit's first draw of the scanned page at preview-pane size (920×1300 px) takes **76–496 ms, median about 180 ms** (s1 89, s3 78, s4 115, s5 93, s6 76, s10 172, s11 194, s2 239, s12 358, s7 453, s8 496, s9 489 ms; images up to 3477×4323 px), because the full-resolution scan is decoded on first draw; a PDFView shows an empty page until then. A second draw takes 3–11 ms, and a page copy shares it — but Core Graphics keeps the decoded image only at the resolution drawn: after a warm 920×1300 draw, a 2× draw still cost 78–707 ms. So warming the document cannot help PDFView's tiles, whose size is not known ahead.
  **Fix:** `PreviewImagePrefetcher` (new, `Views/`) draws the list selection's first image page to a pane-sized bitmap on a background queue as soon as the selection changes — while the reader is still on the list, before Space — and the rows either side while the preview is up (the selection's first two files for a multi-selection). The newest request replaces queued ones (holding ↓ never builds a backlog); 8 bitmaps (about 4 MB each) kept, keyed by path, page and a `stat(2)` file stamp, so a rewritten file is never shown stale. Each render opens its own `PDFDocument` (no PDFKit object crosses threads) and writes nothing. `PlaceholderPageOverlay` shows the bitmap through PDFKit's page overlay, which PDFKit lays out in page space and turns with the page (so the bitmap is drawn unrotated); it steps aside for good on a text selection or find highlights, which PDFKit draws under overlays, and draws nothing when zoomed past its own resolution, leaving PDFKit's sharper render. A bitmap that lands after the page is shown is still taken, only for the page it was drawn from. The preview's image pane identity now includes the file path (↑/↓ reload the model on document 0, pair 0, so `pageIdentity` alone repeated).
  **Before / after:** before, the image appeared 76–496 ms (median ~180 ms) after the text on the sampled scans; after, when the bitmap is drawn ahead it is in hand at once (0.01 ms lookup), so the image appears with the text. If Space follows a click faster than the background render, the first of the two renders to finish shows — never slower than before. The on-screen paint itself could not be timed headless (a PDFView outside a shown window never schedules its tiles), so the figures are PDFKit's page draw at pane size, the same work its tiles do.
  **Verified:** `PreviewImagePrefetchTests` (10): bitmap orientation and fitting, the file left untouched, cache hit / stale-stamp miss / bound / newest-request-wins, the overlay upright over a blank page at all four rotations and gone after retiring, nothing drawn past its resolution, a hosted `PDFPaneView` taking a late bitmap, retiring on PDFKit's own selection notification, and covering a crop box smaller than the media box; `PDFPaneViewportTests` and `DocumentRenderGuardTests` green. Reader unit bundle 635 tests green (DeepLinkTests skipped as usual), no new warnings. VM XCUITest: the five preview tests passed (open/dismiss, text pane, Fit Page, non-PDF image, ⌘C); screenshots show the image pane drawn at fit and sharp when zoomed. Review (Opus): no high findings; applied — redraw the overlay on zoom, a per-view key so an outgoing view never draws the next file's bitmap, a cheap check before reading the selection, one shared key format, the hosted test.
  **Limits:** only pair 0's image page is drawn ahead (a multi-pair document's later pairs load as before); the full document window is unchanged; every list click now costs one background decode (76–496 ms of one core). No bench cache used; the scratch copies were deleted.

- [x] **W40.fix-reader-restore-scroll — a relaunch returns to the rows the user was looking at [S · S3]** · §W40 · SHIPPED 2026-11-06 (this commit) (lane: reader) (uses: build,vm) — Found by the owner's Reader guided session 1, 2026-11-04 (`verification/sessions/reader-1-returned.md`, row 35); the owner's call: fix everything on the form, in his priority order. After a quit and relaunch the window came back to the right smart folder but, the owner thinks, not to the same place in it. Restore the scroll position and selection with the folder.
  **Cause.** The owner was right. The selection was saved and restored (`lastSelectionFileURLs`), but nothing scrolled to it, and the scroll position was never saved, so a relaunch opened at the top of the list with the selected rows possibly off screen.
  **Fix.** The table reports the row under the list's top edge after each scroll (clip-view bounds, `AppKitTableView.Coordinator.observeScrolling`); `NavigationModel.noteTopVisibleRow` saves it as `lastTopRowFileURL`, written once the scrolling stops (0.3 s) and on quit. On the relaunch's resume the model asks the table to put that row back at the top (`scrollTargetAtTop`, `scrollRowToTop`), and asks again on each recompute while rows are still arriving (a smart folder's text search, a cold scan: the table keeps its offset, not its row). That stops once the user scrolls (wheel, scroller, gesture), clicks or types in the list, once the folder, filter or sort changes, or once the row is no longer listed. Saving is ignored until the place is restored, so the first unscrolled draw cannot overwrite it. With no saved row still listed, the restored selection is scrolled into view. No migration (nothing to migrate).
  **Tests.** `RestoreListPlaceTests` (unit, 5): the saved row comes back at the top; the first draw and the restore do not overwrite it; recomputes keep it until the user moves; a filter change drops it; with no saved row the selection is shown. `RestoreScrollUITests` (VM): an 80-file scratch corpus scrolled by the wheel to doc-22/23, ⌘Q, relaunch; it comes back with doc-22 at the top (screenshots `restore-scroll-before-quit` / `-after-relaunch` read). The saved row is the one under the top edge, which may have been half hidden before the quit, so the place is exact to within one row. Reader unit bundle green, no new warnings. No bench cache used.

  From the owner's Reader guided session 1 (2026-11-04, row 33); the owner chose Finder-style rule rows at the 2026-11-04 walkthrough (W40.reader-advanced-search-owner-ok), with starter rows (OCR text, Tags, Date) and "has none of these tags" in Advanced Search only — the filter bar keeps its no-NOT rule.
  **What it is.** `Core/AdvancedSearch.swift`: a rule tree — "all"/"any of the following rules", rows of field · operator · value, and nested groups with their own any/all. Fields: Any text (OCR text, name, classification) and OCR text only (contains all of / the phrase / any of / none of; a trailing `*` is a prefix), File name (contains / does not contain / begins / ends with), Tags (has all / any / none of, by tag identity), Quality (one of / none of, with "no quality tag"), Read state, Date (between / on or after / on or before / missing; a year, month, day or decade; either date, own or sent-with), Folder (inside / not inside, on a path-component boundary), Needs attention, Ambiguous date, Flagged. An empty row is inactive and skipped, so the starter rows match everything until filled in. Text rules become quoted FTS5 expressions (`ContentIndex.search(expression:)`, `searchRanked(expression:)`, `snippets(expression:)`); no typed text can be FTS5 syntax (quotes doubled, `NEAR`/`:`/`OR` quoted, punctuation-only tokens dropped).
  **Smart folders are rule trees.** `SavedSearch` = name + `AdvancedSearch` (it held a `LibraryFilter` and a Find query). Saving the filter bar stores its state as the equivalent rules narrowed onto the open folder (`NavigationModel.effectiveSearch`; an "any" folder becomes a group), so what is saved is what the list shows — the old per-facet `LibraryFilter.effective` merge, which could save something else, is deleted with its tests. An Advanced Search run unsaved is the same base scope (filter bar on top, Clear back to it, survives relaunch). Text rules run one index query each (a lone positive rule reuses the ranked query); the list sorts by their relevance while Find is empty and the top 300 hits get snippets (no fill-in past those — the Find box keeps its fill). Folder rules outside the current root are left out with a status note. Sidebar counts skip folders with text rules, as before, and refresh for flag and needs-attention changes. The store loads entries one at a time, so an old-shape entry is dropped alone. No migration is written because there is nothing to migrate (owner, 2026-08-01).
  **The form.** `Views/AdvancedSearchSheet.swift`: rule rows with field and operator popups, −/+ and a group button; a tag token field, quality checkboxes, date fields that turn red when unreadable, a folder chooser; a live count; Search, Save as Smart Folder…, and Edit Smart Folder… (sidebar menu) opening the same sheet filled in and saving in place. Reached by Advanced… beside the OCR box, the Saved menu, and Selection ▸ Advanced Search… (⇧⌥⌘F; ⌥⌘F stays Search OCR Text).

Also fixed: an emptied group could not be refilled (a group now keeps one row; its own − removes it), counts and Save used folder rules the list had dropped, file-name rules ignored accents where the filter bar does not.
  **Tests.** `AdvancedSearchTests` (15: every operator, dates by precision and role, groups, the filter-bar conversion matching `LibraryFilter.matches` row for row, narrowing, lenient decode, FTS expressions and the text rules against a real FTS5 index); `AdvancedSearchScopeTests` (the model end to end on a scratch fixture with a real index: unsaved scope, relevance and snippets, filter bar on top, save, rename, edit, Flagged following a flag, counts, delete); `SavedSearchStoreTests` (+2: update in place, an unreadable entry dropped alone). `AdvancedSearchUITests` in the Tart VM: starter rows, field and operator popups, the count following a rule, + and −, Search, Save as Smart Folder, Edit Smart Folder filled in; screenshots `w40-advanced-search-starter/-filled/-edit` read (the first run's form clipped on both sides; widened and re-checked). The owner also asks for one live selection at a time: selecting in one pane clears the other, so it is never ambiguous what a copy takes. Copy (⌘C), Copy Cleaned for Prose (⌥⌘C) and the services all act on the pane that holds the selection. Reproduce first, on a scratch copy. Cause, read from the code and shown by the new tests: a one-page PDF (almost all of the corpus) has no OCR text page, so its right pane was a selectable SwiftUI `Text` whose selection nothing could read; Copy and Copy Cleaned took the image page's selection, and Edit ▸ Copy, validated by the image pane's PDFView, was off. The pane is now a read-only AppKit text view (`ExtractedTextPane` + `ExtractedTextController`, `ExtractedTextView`), so ⌘C, ⌥⌘C and the system services take its selection; its own Copy writes plain text (an NSTextView would also put the find highlights on the pasteboard as rich text). One live selection: a selection the user makes in a pane (the pane is first responder, so find's hit is not counted) moves the focus border there and clears the other pane's, on one-page PDFs and two-page pairs alike; copies read the focused pane first. Find's highlights stay attributes on the text, so they never touch the selection, and the current hit now scrolls into view. Focus Text Page puts the caret in the text pane on a one-page PDF too. Tests: `DocumentCopyTextPaneTests` (8, including a render guard that the pane draws its text), the find-highlight test and the text-size layout test moved to the text view; the whole unit bundle (DeepLinkTests skipped as usual) passes, no new warnings. The risk is the saved shape: `SavedSearchStore.load` drops any entry this build cannot decode, and the next add, rename, move or delete saves the shorter list over the old one, so a change to `SavedSearch`, `AdvancedSearch` or `LibraryFilter` that is not decode-compatible loses Smart Folders silently. The fixture is never regenerated: a later format adds a new fixture beside it, and each must still load. (2) No silent loss: when `load` drops an entry, keep the raw bytes of the whole list under a second key (`savedSearches.unreadable`, never overwritten while it holds data) and tell the user once, in the sidebar, how many Smart Folders could not be read.   SHIPPED 2026-11-11, $0. Format ▸ Underline (⌘U) and Highlight (⇧⌘H), and two formatting-bar buttons beside Italic. **How each is written:** CommonMark has neither, so underline is `<u>…</u>` and highlight `<mark>…</mark>`, the HTML tags most Markdown renderers show (`==` was the other candidate; GitHub and Apple's parser read it as text, while both tags come back from Apple's parser as inline-HTML runs of their own, measured). Tags sit outside a run's link, code and emphasis (`<u><mark>**two**</mark></u>`; Apple reads no HTML inside link text, measured) and start and end where the style does, so bold with edge spaces inside underline is stable on the second save. On reopen `InlineTagStyle.applyTags` pairs the tags within a paragraph and removes them; an unpaired or empty pair stays raw HTML as before. A typed `<` that could start a tag or autolink is now written `\<`, so a typed `<u>` stays text (`a < b` and `3<4` are unchanged). The highlight is its own key (`noteHighlight`), its yellow shown again after a list, heading or inline-code change clears the background; the toggles do nothing in a code block, whose text is written without tags. Extract titles and the search index drop the tags (a search for "mark" no longer finds every highlighted note); a save made while an input method is composing leaves out its composing underline. **Round-trips through quit and reopen:** `UnderlineHighlightTests` (18 tests) saves through `NotesModel.setBody`, reloads with a fresh `NoteStore` over the same folder and checks the text, both styles' exact ranges and that a second save changes nothing; also headings, lists, quotes, links, code spans, images, undo and typing after the toggle. Tier-2 adversarial review (Opus): no text loss found; its six findings (edge-space instability, code-block toggles, the search index, an escaped backslash in titles, a hand-written empty pair, input-method underline) all fixed, the first five with tests. Notes unit bundle 1,203 tests green, no new warnings. Not checked in pixels: the underline and yellow are AppKit's own drawing of `.underlineStyle` and `.backgroundColor`, and no VM run was made for the two buttons. `MarkdownBridgeTests.unsupportedAttributeMidParagraph…` now uses strikethrough, since underline is supported. Rebuild the cleaner on line geometry: take the lines from `selectionsByLine()` themselves (splitting an embedded newline), and classify each block from indent, gap and marker: paragraph (first-line indent, a gap, a short line ending a sentence), list item with its level (markers `1.`, `(a)`, `a)`, `•`, `–`, `*`; hanging or first-line-indented continuation lines joined to their item), heading (a short line set apart, often in capitals). Output keeps one item per line with its marker and indents sub-items; de-hyphenation stays. A line wholly in capitals becomes title case, with acronyms and initials kept (UCLA, M/D, J. W.) and small words lower inside; capitals inside a mixed-case sentence are left. The title-case rule goes into ArchiveCore, shared with W47.ct-normalise. The text pane (no geometry) gets the same treatment from its line breaks. Tests on synthetic fixtures that reproduce both pages' geometry (the repo is public: no corpus text in fixtures), plus a local check on the two scratch copies whose result goes in the DONE entry as counts (paragraphs, list items, levels).

Rows come from `selectionsByLine()` themselves, with two repairs measured on the Bower pages: text before an embedded newline is the tail of the previous line's word (the OCR wrote "adhering" whole at a line end; the selection reads "ing⏎to the…"), glued only when it starts lower case onto a letter; selections side by side on one baseline under four line heights apart are one row (a marker "(c)" that is its own selection). A rows-vs-text word-sequence check, space for space, sends anything that does not match to the text-only path, and `assemble` refuses any result whose letters (case, whitespace and hyphens aside) differ from the selection's. Each block is sorted into paragraphs (gap, first-line indent, short line ending a sentence, as before), list items (markers `1.` `1)` `(1)` `a.` `a)` `(a)` `iv.` `(iv)`, glyph bullets, dashes; a dash, letter or number only after a line that ended or a colon, at an indent of its own, or in an open list; level from indent and a new marker style) and headings (short, set apart by capitals unless most of the block is in capitals, centring, or gaps). Items come out one per line, sub-items four spaces a level. The text pane gets the same pass from its line breaks and leading spaces (blank lines kept). `ArchiveCore/Text/TitleCase.swift` (`TitleCase.titleCased(_:keeping:)`, `isAllCapitals`) for W47.ct-normalise too: acronyms (a short list plus no-vowel words), initials, M/D, AT&T, Roman numerals kept; small words lower inside, also inside compounds (Commander-in-Chief); capital after a sentence end and a colon; Mr./Lt./Sgt. as titles; only letter case changes. New Options toggle "Title-case text in capitals", on.
  - **A judgement on the spec.** Title case is applied to headings, list items and one-line units; prose of several lines wholly in capitals (a cable, a telegram) is copied as written, since title case on quoted prose is worse than capitals (the review's finding). - [x] **W44.reocr-header-longname — the header parser misses the reader line under a long filename [S · ~1 session · Tier-2]** · §Reader ↔ Processor — flag poor OCR and read it again with a better reader · SHIPPED 2026-11-12
  Core `PDFHeaderParser.parse` now finds provenance under an original filename that PDFKit reads back as three or more lines. The longer scan runs only when header slots 1–3 hold no provenance candidate, so nothing that parsed before can change. Each filename line must be nonempty, not a field after the first line, and free of ` · `. Together the lines are at most 255 UTF-8 bytes, the last ends in an extension, and the next line must be well-formed provenance. Anything else leaves provenance missing; it never searches the body. The SPEC (§"One structured header parse", and the ambiguity paragraph) states the rule and the new limit: a page with no provenance whose body opens like a filename followed by a provenance-looking line is read as header.
  **Tests.** Core `ReOCRHeaderTests.testLongFilenameOfManyLinesKeepsProvenanceWithoutReadingTheBody` covers a 4-line name, an opaque `Kind:` first slot, the 255/256-byte edge and six refusals. Reader `ContentIndexTests.testLongFilenameOverSeveralLinesKeepsTheProviderInTheReader` goes through `PDFTextExtractor`. The Processor `ReOCRPairsTestDriver` case 3 now expects the real PDFGenerator output with an 82-character underscored name to be read and kept on the replacement page. All `test-reocr-*.sh` drivers report ALL PASS.
  **Review.** Tier-2 adversarial review (Opus) traced every path and confirmed no previously parsed input changes. It found one wrong test assertion, which is fixed, and flagged the low-severity false positive now stated in the SPEC. No migration was written because there is no app-produced material to migrate.

- [x] **W44.reocr-reader — flag poor OCR in the Reader and hand it to the Processor [M · ~1-2 sessions · Tier-2]** · §Reader ↔ Processor — flag poor OCR and read it again with a better reader · SHIPPED 2026-11-13
  One session, $0. **What the Reader does now.** Tags ▸ Flag as Poor OCR / Remove Poor OCR Flag (⌃⌘P; the title follows the selection), also in the row menu and the document window, for one or many files: the `OCR Poor` subject through the same `TagWriter` delta, ledger group and undo as any tag edit, run off the main thread. Sort & Filter ▸ Show Poor OCR Only (`LibraryFilter.poorOCROnly`, optional so saved smart folders still decode; a smart folder saved from it is the tag rule). Tags ▸ Improve OCR… hands the selection to the Processor's dialog: `archiveprocessor://improve-ocr` inline up to 8 files, else a manifest staged with inode, size and SHA-256 (`ImproveOCRManifest.stage`, ArchiveCore); without an installed Processor it says so. File ▸ Connect Improve OCR Folder… (the Reader's own security-scoped bookmark; the store ID checked on every use). The document window's status bar shows the text page's reader and Kind from its header. The Processor's receipts re-index a replaced file regardless of its kept date (`ContentIndexer.forget` + the ordinary pass) and reload a document window showing it on the same pair.
  **The flag protocol.** Every TagWriter write whose delta names the tag (Flag/Unflag, a subject edit, rename, undo, redo) runs `PoorOCRFlagGuard`: the file's flag lock before coordination, `begin`, the write, `commit` of what reads back; a dead barrier is reconciled first; after the tag write nothing throws, an unfinished record is reconciled and reported. A file's archive is the nearest root marker above it, in both apps now (the Processor's `findRoot` stops at an unreadable marker too). Never connected: a generic edit goes ahead unrecorded, like Finder; connected but unusable: refused with the reason.
  **Processor changes (shared protocol).** `ReOCRJob.clearFlag`/`reflag` reconcile a dead barrier under the lock and treat the review as out of date, instead of refusing forever; `ImproveOCRRequestStore` names manifests through `ImproveOCRManifest.url(for:in:)`.
  **Review.** Tier-2 adversarial review (Opus), two passes. Pass 1: HIGH — a record failure after the tag write reported a refusal, leaving a change on disk with no ledger line or undo (fixed: nothing after the write throws); MEDIUM — the two apps keyed files under different roots with nested markers (fixed: nearest marker in both); MEDIUM — a dead barrier blocked the Processor's clear forever (fixed); LOW — unreadable tag after a failed write recorded clear (now flagged). Pass 2 confirmed those and found MEDIUM — the off-main batch could put an older result over a row a later edit had updated, so the next facet edit computed from a wrong row (fixed: a batch result is shown only while the file still reads as it left it); LOWs folded in. Pass 3 (receipts, viewer, tests, docs): HIGH — a capped seen-list would have re-read and re-indexed an evicted receipt's file at every check once past 5,000 (fixed: uncapped); MEDIUM — the receipt path was built from the granted root's spelling, which can differ from the library's row (symlinked root, decomposed name), so the row was not dropped yet the receipt consumed (fixed: matched to a library row by normalized tail, then full key; marked seen only on a row or a file truly gone); MEDIUM — another archive's receipts were re-scanned every 20 s (fixed: skipped until the library changes); LOWs folded in (an unreadable receipt waits instead of being dropped; the reload hops to the main actor; SPEC §3/§4 wording matches the code).
  **Tests.** Reader `PoorOCRFlagGuardTests` (18: generations, undo, rename, refusals, barrier reconcile, failed write, nearest marker, inline link, private manifest, two archives, receipts by row in another Unicode spelling, gone/foreign/unreadable receipts, uncapped seen list, filter), `DocumentViewerPagePairTests`, `ReaderCommandTableTests`, `ContentIndexTests`, `DocumentRenderGuardTests`, `FlagColumnRefreshTests` green; VM `ImproveOCRUITests.testFlagFilterHandOffAndUnflag` (⌃⌘P writes the tag and its shared record, the filter lists it alone, Improve OCR… hands it over via the DEBUG recorder, the Remove title, the second ⌃⌘P). Processor `test-reocr-job.sh` and `test-reocr-request-store.sh` ALL PASS; Reader, Processor and Notes build with no new warnings; write-surface lint clean, self-test 25/25.   SHIPPED 2026-11-13, $0, one session. **The pause is lifted** (`AUTONOMOUS_GUI_VM_PAUSED` defaults to empty; prove-gui-vm.sh's pause checks now prove that unset means not paused). **The gate runs one chunk per invocation.** On the 27.2 guest no whole lane fits. The rest of the gate measured 1,353–1,466 s of the engine's 3,000 s on 2026-11-12, so the VM step gets a 1,400 s budget (`AUTONOMOUS_GUI_VM_BUDGET`). Each invocation does this: one `build-for-testing`; `tart_enumerate_tests` (tart-lib.sh, which the runner's `VM_SPLIT` now uses too); then one chunk with `test-without-building`, rotating over app × chunk.   **Chunks are planned by measured time.** `ops/gui/vm-chunks.py` caps each chunk at `AUTONOMOUS_GUI_VM_CHUNK` estimated seconds (600). It uses whole classes, and splits a class into its tests only when the class alone is over the budget (Notes' NotesGUITests 1,335 s and LayoutGuardUITests 1,202 s). The estimates come from the committed seed `ops/gui/vm-test-times.tsv`: Notes from the 2026-11-12 fresh-guest chunks; Reader and Processor from the 2026-11-06 27.2 baseline, which had harness failures, so those figures overstate and the chunks come out smaller. The gate's learned times from passed tests override the seed (`.maintenance/gui-vm-test-times.tsv`). A test with no measurement counts as 40 s. A plan is made at an app's chunk 0 and kept for the rest of its cycle (`.maintenance/gui-vm-plan-<app>`), so a cycle runs every test once. A test added mid-cycle goes into the plan's last chunk, and a selector that no longer matches anything is dropped. The runner's `VM_SPLIT=N` now plans at most N chunks with the same planner, by time rather than by class count. A cycle is Notes 13 chunks + Reader 9 + Processor about 2, roughly 24 invocations.
  **Retry:** the retry reruns only the failed tests' classes, and only when attempt 1 has every test of the chunk reported, no crash report and no runner restart; otherwise it reruns the whole chunk. A retry the budget cannot fit is SKIPPED, not RED, with attempt 1's failures kept in the LAST-FAILURE log. A RED names the `ONLY_TESTING=… vm-gui-runner.sh` command that reruns its chunk. A compile failure on both build attempts is RED, as before.
  **Done criterion, in the real VM:** the gate script ran by hand from the worktree, under the heavy lock, with its state in /tmp. Notes chunk 1/13: 8 tests passed, GREEN, 631 s for the whole step (build and enumeration about 2 min). Reader chunk 1/9: SnapshotTests plus AccessibilityAuditUITests, so both bundles' summaries; GREEN in 494 s. The engine's own full health gate had not run with the step at ship time; its next run is the first. Its 9 learned times were copied into the primary checkout's `.maintenance/`.

  - A retry that ran out of budget was classed RED, and could push the step past its budget. Now an attempt needs `AUTONOMOUS_GUI_VM_ATTEMPT_FLOOR` (320 s) of cap before its uncapped kill, prerun and fixture steps.
  - A narrowed retry could clear a crash or an unloaded bundle that it never ran again.
  It also found one MED, fixed: a test added mid-cycle went into every remaining chunk.
  Left open (MED): a chunk whose real time always passes its cap ends on maxrun and is SKIPPED every cycle. Its passed tests' times are learned, so the next cycle's plan shrinks; a single test longer than the cap would never finish. A heavy-lock wait does not count against the budget, and does not need to, since the engine does not charge it either.

  unchanged. Each window remembers it (`ar.doc.invertImages`, `ar.preview.invertImages`), as it does the thumbnails.

  the selection's text are untouched; the tiles draw a filtered bitmap (cached, 400 at most).
  Chosen by trying both on corpus pages (read-only renders in /tmp: a typed page, a purple ditto syllabus, a
  typed table, a printed cover with a seal): a dimmed view (×0.5 after levels) keeps the look but halves the contrast
  and leaves the paper the brightest thing on screen; the inversion reads better, paper near black and ink near
  white. Three details make it work: it is done on sRGB values through `CIColorCubeWithColorSpace` (Core Image's
  linear light turned the photographed pages' 0.7 grey paper into a light grey, measured: a page's mean went 0.63 to
  0.81 under a plain `CIColorInvert`); the hue is kept (only the HSL lightness turns, so ditto ink stays purple);
  and 0.22…0.78 is stretched first and the result kept in 0.10…0.88, since the scans' paper is grey, not white. The
  pane's backdrop is given a grey that draws about 0.32, lighter than any inverted page, so the page edge shows.
  Verified: `DarkPageImagesTests` (the mapping, the filter on a scan-like picture, the pane switching its filter on
  and off in place, a tile render guard), the whole Reader unit bundle; `InvertImagesUITests` in the Tart VM reads

  to 1.2 em for one or two, so a double-spaced typescript (23.3 pt between 9.5 pt lines) read as a paragraph gap

  rows (no page spacing passed) are unchanged. Tests in `CopyTextCleanerTests`: the owner's two selections as
  fixture geometry (one paragraph with the page's spacing, the old `\n\n` without it), a single-spaced two-line
  selection across a blank-line gap still splits, the spacing measure, and an end-to-end PDFKit double-spaced page

(2) **Start warns.** Process Files' Start (button and ⌘R) asks "Run anyway / Cancel" when the output collection has the switch and the run would send pages where they may train: the reader (Local Agent plan, else gateway, else key), Apple Vision's judgement pass, each kind's own reader, the cascade's escalation, a refused page's second readers (Claude plan, Qwen3.6 27B on Chutes, a Mistral key) and the window segmenter's voters (plan or key as the run picks them). The Gemini CLI (may train, unanswerable) and a gateway other than Stanford's (unknown) warn too. (3) **The other pickers take the switch.** `SegmentationApproach.preferredDefault` reads the general layer's switch and answers (`SegmentationRoutes.noTraining/trainingOff`, set in `currentPreselecting`); Improve OCR resolves each file's collection (its folder or the nearest above holding settings, stopping at the root marker) for `noTraining` and `staysOnMac` (the latter only where a layer set it, so a user who never answered keeps the online readers) and passes them to `ReOCRRanking.rank`. (4) **A key can be billed.** A general-only `trainingOff` setting (`key:gemini`, `key:mistral`, `plan:claude`, `plan:chatgpt`; ArchiveCore's vocabulary has its label and words) is asked in the general interview for the keys and plans found; `SettingsTraining.safe` lifts only "unless paid" and "unless opted out", never "may train" or "unknown". Tier-2: an Opus adversarial review found every OpenRouter request goes through the provider field and resumes keep the switch; its findings are fixed (the deny no longer outlives an idle Process Files run or a freed Live Capture processor; Vision's judgement, page-kind readers, cascade and refusal fallback added to the warning; a non-Stanford gateway and the Gemini CLI no longer count as safe; a misplaced ArchiveCore doc comment). Cause, in the app and not the test: the model cleared its snippets correctly (`removeFilter(.text)` empties `ftsSnippets`, and `searchSnippet` returns nil without a query), but clearing keeps the smart folder's row IDs, so `AppKitTableView.updateNSView` took its "IDs unchanged" path and reloaded only `rows(in: visibleRect)`. The fixture's 10 snippet rows (about 50 pt each) overflow the list, and NSTableView keeps row views prepared past the visible rect. Those were never reloaded, kept the old snippet, and came on screen as the reloaded rows shrank; they are also in the accessibility tree the test reads. Fix: a `loadedRows(of:)` helper (`enumerateAvailableRowViews`) now gives the rows to reload on that path, which also calls `noteHeightOfRows`. The snippet-fill reload and the type-marker colour reload use the same set. Verified: in the VM, all 6 `AdvancedSearchUITests` pass, including this test; screenshot `uitest-smart-folder-cleared-search.png` checked by eye (10 compact rows, plain filenames). The Reader unit bundle passes (902 tests, 6 skipped, DeepLinkTests skipped as usual), with no new warnings. KNOWN_ISSUES has a note under the smart-folders entry. No bench cache used.

- [x] **W47.gateway-key-rewrites — find what keeps modifying the Gateway Keychain item [S]** · §Archival containers — W47 (owner, 2026-10-21) · (lane: suite) — 2026-11-12 walkthrough: the item (com.archiveprocessor.app / Gateway) was modified at 17:56 and 22:27 on 2026-11-12, each write resetting its partition list so /usr/bin/security prompts and gateway bench arms stop. SHIPPED 2026-11-19.
  The writer was the Processor app itself. OCRView's `onChange(of: apiKey)` saved the field's value to the Keychain under the current route's account (Gateway, or the provider's), but nothing in that view edits the key: no control binds `$apiKey`, and only `reloadAPIKey()` sets it, from the Keychain, at launch and on every route, local-model or Apple Vision switch. So each launch and switch wrote the stored key back over itself, and a read that came back empty (a denied or locked Keychain) deleted the key. Found by reading code and the unified log, never the secret: the Gateway item's mdat (attributes only) was 2026-11-16 23:36:52Z, ten seconds after an ArchiveProcessor launch at 15:36:42 local with no engine session running (weekly window stop), and Gemini's mdat 23:38:21Z followed; on 2026-11-12 an ArchiveProcessor process started at 17:55, a minute before the 17:56 write. The 2026-11-18 07:23 repair (keychain-partition-fixed) recorded the same mdat, so nothing has written the item since. Fix: the handler is removed (keys are edited in Settings and the key wizard, which already save themselves), and `KeychainHelper.save` no longer writes a value equal to the stored one, which covers the wizard re-validating a saved key and Drive re-saving an unchanged refresh token. Processor Debug build clean (only VisionOCRKit's four existing warnings). No Keychain test: the unit host would touch the real login Keychain. fix-keychain-access.sh not run. $0. No bench cache.
  <!-- /W47.gateway-key-rewrites -->

- [x] **W49.reader-find-word-align — Find pairs hits in the two panes by aligning their words [M]** · §Known limits are queued, accepted or asked (owner, 2026-11-19) — SHIPPED 2026-11-20 (lane: reader). Owner, 2026-11-19 (call 21, accepted-issues sheet entry `r-word-pairing`): change it. Find no longer pairs the image pane's k-th match with the text pane's k-th: `DocumentFindScanner.pairHits` takes each match's offset from PDFKit's own selection, and `FindWordAlignment` cuts both pages into case/diacritic/width-folded words, diffs them (`CollectionDifference` over interned ids) and pairs a match with the match on the word its own word lines up with (the n-th on a word with the n-th on its partner); a match on a word the diff could not line up (a misread "thee") pairs in order with the other page's unpaired match in the same stretch between shared words; anything left is a hit of its pane alone. So a word the text layer split or missed is a text-pane-only hit and later hits stay on the same word in both panes. Pairs whose panes do not both match skip the diff. `FindNavigator(hits:)` takes the paired hits; the count-based init stays as ordinal pairing. Cost (owner asked): a 300-page document of ~600-word pages with a damaged image layer, 9,908 matches: find alone 0.558 s, find + alignment 0.568 s; two unrelated 1,500-word pages 0.046 s (app-hosted unit bundle). KNOWN_ISSUES: the ordinal bullet replaced by the residual ambiguity among identical neighbours (accepted: nothing in the texts tells the copies apart). Tests: `FindWordAlignmentTests` (11: split, missed, image-only, identical, in-word, normalised, offsets, misread stretch, unrelated, PDFKit end to end through the model, the cost), `DocumentViewerPagePairTests` both-panes fixture pinned with a shared trailing word (the old one had two equally good alignments); full Reader unit bundle green (1023, DeepLinkTests skipped as usual). - [x] **W49.proc-resume-standard-runs — a standard Files run resumes after a quit or crash [M]** · §Known limits are queued, accepted or asked … SHIPPED 2026-11-20. Owner, 2026-11-20 walkthrough of 08:05 (call 27), from ArchiveProcessor/POTENTIAL_FEATURES.md. **Finding first: the resume the item asked for already existed**, and the backlog line it came from was stale. A standard (non-batch) Files run writes `PendingRun` to `~/Library/Application Support/ArchiveProcessor/pending_run.json` before its first OCR request (ordered inputs, output folder, backend, and a fingerprinted snapshot of every run setting), then adds each page's reading and the exact output path it was given as the page lands (`saveResultToPendingRun`, after the PDF is written). Quit, crash and Stop all keep the file; at launch the Interrupted Run box offers Resume Run, which replays the run's own snapshot, reuses every saved reading and output (rebuilding only a missing PDF from the saved reading), reads only the pages not in the manifest, then tags and organizes; the file goes when the run finishes or is dismissed. A failed page counts as tried and goes to the end-of-pass retry, not the main pass. Pre-OCRed input keeps no manifest (it buys no OCR). **What this item added, for "a sleep, quit or crash should cost one file at most":** (1) **Quit asks** (`ProcessorAppDelegate`, new): while a run is in its main OCR pass, ⌘Q offers Quit When Pages Are Saved / Quit Now / Cancel. Waiting makes the OCR loops start no new page (`quitWhenPagesSaved`, the four loops in `performOCRParallel`/`performOCRSequential`/`performOCRPhaseForIndices`); when the pass ends, `finishQuitDrainIfAsked` runs Stop (manifest kept) and quits once the run has unwound, so a quit costs nothing. Outside the OCR pass it offers Quit / Cancel. If the pass ends while the alert is up, the question is asked again as it then stands (the Tier-2 review's MED finding). Stop pressed while the quit waits takes the quit back. (2) **Sleep**: `ProcessInfo.beginActivity` holds App Nap off while a run works and idle sleep off during its OCR pass, not while it waits on a review sheet (review LOW-3). (3) **The input folder changed in between**: the resume reads the run's own file list, never the folder. A page not yet read whose file is gone is named in the Interrupted Run box (`pendingRunMissingNote`), and `performOCRCallUntracked` now fails a missing file (`source_missing`) before any route or rotation call, so nothing is sent for it; a file added since is not part of the run; a file replaced at the same path keeps its saved reading if already read and is read as it is now if not; a completed page whose source and output are both gone is restored without its PDF (pre-existing). (4) README §"Interrupted runs" says all of this for users. **Still lost, in KNOWN_ISSUES:** Stop drops the pages in flight and the mixed-PDF and batch routes get no wait on quit (queued: W49.proc-stop-saves-inflight); a crash loses the pages in flight, at most one per OCR worker (accepted, platform fact); a crash during tagging buys tagging's text calls again (queued: W49.proc-resume-tagging-progress, behind nice-to-have). Live Capture keeps its own staging-manifest resume and is not part of the quit question. **Verified:** new key-free contract `scripts/test-run-quit-resume.sh` (`RunQuitResumeContract`, 17 checks through the real `resumeRun` over the injected transport, two workers: no page started after the quit, every page in flight saved, the app quits once, the next resume reads only the rest with one PDF per page, Stop takes the quit back, the missing-page note and guard, the sleep hold) 3/3 ALL PASS after its wait bound went from 15 s to 60 s (one run under another session's Notes test took over 15 s to send its first page); test-batch-resume, test-institutional-compute-import, test-retry-backend, test-ocr-refusal, test-ocr-cascade ALL PASS; an Explore pass found all 21 `performOCRCall` sites pass an existing file. - [x] **W49.reader-undo-after-crash — undo history survives a crash, except for the files the crashed action touched [M]** · §Known limits are queued, accepted or asked — Owner call 22, 2026-11-19 (`17b-accepted-review-round2.json` entry `r-crash-undo`). SHIPPED 2026-11-20. Each `actionIntent` now carries `files` (path + device/inode the action expects to write; bulk callers declare them through `withContext(files:)`, so a bulk intent is still one F_FULLFSYNC), `extends` (an undeclared file gets its own synchronized intent before its write) and `launch` (the writing process). After a crash an unclosed action counts as complete when every listed file has its record, no other change by the same process touched those files after it began, and each file is still the recorded object reading as its newest record's after-state (proof cached per ledger object and line count). Otherwise the action, every older change to its files, every change to them by its process and, transitively, whatever those withheld groups touched are left out; older actions on other files stay undoable. A running action is never offered; an intent without `files` is still a full barrier; `actionDone` is appended under the journal's open lock. No migration was written because there is nothing to migrate. The ledger is the Reader's own file, not a cross-app contract, so its format is documented in `ArchiveReader/REFERENCE.md` §12 and KNOWN_ISSUES §W40.audit-ledger-undo rather than `SPEC/`. Tier-2: an adversarial review (Opus) found two HIGH paths. The concurrent-action one is fixed with the launch ID; a second pass found retry groups (no intent, so no launch) slipping past it and a stale proof cache, both fixed. The failed extending intent is documented with the accepted double fault, since a ledger failure never fails a tag write. Its MED findings (early stop at a barrier, close race, interleaved rewrite fooling the proof, cost of re-proving, inode-first listing) are fixed. LedgerJournalTests gained 10 crash-scenario tests; the full Reader unit bundle is green (1,066 tests, 0 failures). No bench cache used.
  <!-- /W49.reader-undo-after-crash -->
